California AB 1978 Janitorial Licensing and Cal/OSHA Rules

Every commercial janitorial contractor working in Chula Vista—whether a regional San Diego firm or a small family-owned crew—is legally bound by **California AB 1978 (Property Service Workers Protection Act)**. Contractors must hold an active California Department of Industrial Relations (DIR) janitorial registration, carry valid California Workers' Compensation, and complete mandatory biennial sexual-harassment prevention training for all covered employees.

faqs.q: Why must Chula Vista cleaning vendors carry California AB 1978 registration?
faqs.a: California AB 1978 requires every janitorial employer in the state to register annually with the DIR, verify Workers' Compensation coverage, and complete mandatory employee harassment-prevention training. Hiring an unregistered vendor exposes your company to civil liability.

faqs.q: Is Chula Vista cheaper for office cleaning than downtown San Diego or Irvine?
faqs.a: Yes, slightly. Chula Vista's 1.15x multiplier ($40–$69/hr) sits roughly 7% below Irvine (1.23x, $43–$74/hr) because South Bay parking, staging access, and suburban business-park logistics avoid high-rise tower delays.

faqs.q: Should paper towels, toilet paper, and liners be bundled into a Chula Vista janitorial quote?
faqs.a: Usually it is cheaper to purchase bulk paper and soap directly and pay labor-only cleaning rates. If bundled by the janitorial vendor, expect consumables to add roughly $0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit.

faqs.q: What services are excluded from standard Chula Vista recurring cleaning rates?
